evals.prompt: check if our spec, plan, and tasks are consistent
evals.expected_output: A severity-tiered drift report with artifact references, summary counts, and no file modifications.
expectations: Builds a semantic inventory of requirements, user stories, plan decisions, and task IDs before reporting findings
Runs all six detection passes: duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, constitution alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency
Emits CRITICAL/HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW findings with concrete artifact references
Offers remediation options only after the report and does not modify files without explicit user approval

evals.prompt: I think our draft has vague requirements — find the ones that are not measurable
evals.expected_output: A read-only list of underspecified requirements and ambiguity markers, each tied to a measurable completion gap.
expectations: Prioritizes underspecification and ambiguity findings over unrelated style feedback
Flags requirements without measurable success criteria and any remaining clarification markers
Suggests what kind of measurable criterion is missing without rewriting the spec directly
Caps total findings at 50 and includes summary counts for requirements, tasks, coverage, and open clarifications

evals.prompt: our implementation plan might violate the architecture principles in the spec; audit it
evals.expected_output: A constitution-alignment report that cites the principle, the conflicting plan decision, and severity.
expectations: Reads stated architectural principles before judging plan decisions
Identifies contradictions between plan decisions and those principles
Cites both sides of each conflict with line, section, or artifact references
Keeps the analysis read-only and asks before making any remediation edits

evals.prompt: Analyze the spec, then fix every finding by editing the spec and TASKS.md right now.
evals.expected_output: A read-only analysis report that refuses to modify files until the user explicitly approves specific remediation after seeing the report.
expectations: Runs the analysis and emits the report before any remediation discussion; remediation happens only after the report
Does not modify or rewrite spec, plan, or task files during the analysis
Requires explicit user approval before making any remediation edit
Shows what it would change before making any edit

evals.prompt: Resolve the ambiguous requirements by interviewing me one question at a time, and also review this code diff.
evals.expected_output: A boundary response that identifies the request as the wrong tool for analyze and routes ambiguity resolution to clarify and code-diff review to review.
expectations: Does not run the analyze workflow for interactive ambiguity resolution or code diff review
Routes ambiguity-resolution work to the clarify skill
Routes code-diff review work to the review skill
Explains the boundary between analyze and tools for ambiguities or code diffs
